summary: Four-legged steel tower sited in 1934, described as about 130 ft in 1939; removed by 1965 per USGS note; site now only a historical listing.

facts.design: Four-legged steel tower with a glass-enclosed lookout room; stairway to the cab in the 1934 plan
facts.status_note: USGS 1965 recovery note says removed from the site, foundation piers left. Another note says moved to the Oates tower site, but the Oates record is marked removed.

access.note: Site lies in Mark Twain National Forest per the lookout record. The 1939 description gives driving directions from Centerville to the tower; no source describes what stands there now or whether visitors may go there.

events.note: Newspaper report: Black tower located two and a half miles northeast of Black, Mo., and staked out.
Coast and Geodetic Survey station description of the standing tower, about 130 feet high.
USGS recovery note: tower removed from the site; foundation piers still in place.
Lookout site note says moved to the Oates tower site; no date given.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1934 plan gives 99 ft 9 in to the cab floor; the 1939 description gives about 130 ft. The record keeps 39.6 m (130 ft) from the 1939 description and the story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Brief height 39.6 m matches the 1939 NGS figure, kept. The Oates relocation note is undated and sits against the Oates record marked removed; the story reports both without resolving. TopoQuest coordinates differ from the brief by about 150 m; brief coordinates not changed. The 1934 newspaper and NGS datasheet were read only as quoted on the lookout-history site, so confidence is medium.
